newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries easier in Tokyo on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries easier in Tokyo on profit-taking.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly lower at the Tokyo midday on Monday due to profit-taking after rising sharply in New York on Friday, traders said.
Activity was sluggish due to a lack of fresh market-moving incentives, they said.

Traders said that the market undertone was becoming stronger as speculation of an imminent credit-tightening faded as the results of the U.S. producer price index (PPI), released on Friday, were below earlier forecasts.
"The market should test prices higher, but the pace of the rise was a bit too fast," a Japanese trust bank manager said.
The key 30-year bond stood at 98-20/32, yielding 6.73 percent, compared with 98-22/32 in New York on Friday.
"People are not expecting to see an interest rate hike in July and also many are starting to think that there will not be one in August," another trader said.
"If this mood stays, then I think the market will test the yield of the key 30-year bond below 6.65 percent, and above 113 for the key T-bond futures contract pretty soon," he added.
Traders said that they were particularly waiting for the U.S. consumer price index and industrial production data, both due for release on Tuesday.
The September T-bond futures contract fell 3/32 to 111-24/32 by early afternoon trade from the previous close. It moved in a range of 111-23/32 to 111-26/32.
